significance.justification: If verified true, the claim would establish that the measurable "commitment-lead" between truth-value stabilization and the disambiguating token predictively couples premature internal commitment to later belief-versus-fact errors, and that selectively delaying this commitment causally reduces those errors. This combines a form-(iii) temporal/predictive relation with a form-(ii) mechanism, fixing expectations about which items should fail and why; it is more constraining than static truth-direction results such as Marks and Tegmark's The Geometry of Truth, because the substantive conclusion concerns an ordering and later behavioral consequence rather than merely decodability. The phenomenon and mechanism are determinate, and a negative result—no predictive advantage over final-token confidence and no selective benefit from delaying commitment—would rule out premature commitment as the proposed explanation, although it would not rule out other dynamic accounts of belief. Topic substitution fails: generic research on LLM beliefs would not itself imply the quoted "commitment onset" ordering or its error coupling, so the claim merits above the topic-median score.

reach.justification: The principal handles are the "commitment-lead metric" and the intervention of "causally delaying commitment by suppressing the truth direction until the proposition is fully read." The metric is potentially ex ante because it forecasts a likely answering error during reading, before the answer is produced, while the suppression rule provides an action window; however, practical use may depend on knowing or detecting the proposition's disambiguation point. After per-model re-extraction, the asserted relation—earlier commitment relative to disambiguation predicts more errors—still predicts what should be found across "several open-weight models," so more than a model-specific search procedure transfers, with likely uptake by model auditors and developers rather than only belief researchers. Topic substitution again fails because the topic alone supplies neither this temporal predictor nor the suppression rule, but the claim stops short of asserting a tokenizer-, architecture-, and item-independent quantitative law, limiting it to the lower end of the 7–8 band.
